html:
Gurkhas are soldiers from Nepal recruited into the British and Indian armies since 1815, named after the hill kingdom of Gorkha, home of the Shah kings.

During the Anglo-Nepalese War the British were so impressed by their enemies that they began to recruit them, mostly men of the Gurung, Magar, Rai and Limbu peoples. Gurkhas fought for Britain in the rebellion of 1857, in both world wars and in many later wars, and won a long list of Victoria Crosses.

At the split of India in 1947 the regiments were divided between Britain and India. Army pay and pensions were for generations a main source of cash in the hills, a forerunner of the mass labour migration that now sends Nepalis to the Gulf and Malaysia. Britain gave Gurkha veterans the right to settle there in 2009.
sum: Gurkhas are soldiers from Nepal recruited into the British and Indian armies since 1815, named after the hill kingdom of Gorkha, home of the Shah kings.
